Device Provisioning

Build a new appliance machine step by step (address, DNS name, virtual machine, power-on, registration) as a recorded run that can be preflighted and rolled back.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsoperations.view operations.apply
📍 WhereAdministrator → Devices → Device Provisioning (URL /device-provisioning/), in every ADOM; Automation → Device Provisioning without users.manage

What is it?#

Device Provisioning builds an appliance that does not exist yet. Each build is a run: SATOM reserves a management address, publishes a DNS name, creates and powers on a virtual machine on a registered hypervisor, checks that the address answers, and registers the result as an appliance. Every step is written to the run log, so a half-finished run can be rolled back from what it recorded.

It is the counterpart of System Provisioning, which pushes system configuration to appliances that already exist.

What does it do?#

  • Offers five modes that decide how much of the pipeline a run performs (see Modes).
  • Preflight asks the hypervisor what it can actually do and lists blockers and warnings before anything changes.
  • Run walks the mode's plan; a run refuses to start when preflight reports a blocker.
  • Roll back undoes, in reverse, only what the run recorded creating: the virtual machine, the DNS record and an IPAM-allocated address.
  • Runs are scoped to the ADOM they were created in. A run started in the FortiADC ADOM is invisible from the FortiWeb ADOM, and opening its URL there returns 404 Not Found.
  1. 1Create runname, mode, hypervisor, address, sizing
  2. 2Preflightplan, blockers and warnings; changes nothing
  3. 3Runexecutes the planned steps and logs each one
  4. 4Paused / failedread the reason, act on it, press Resume or Run
  5. 5Done or Roll backappliance registered, or recorded artefacts removed

Requirements#

  • For every mode except Config only: at least one enabled hypervisor registered by an administrator in Settings › Hypervisors (Proxmox or ESXi). Disabled hypervisors are not offered.
  • Optional: an install image uploaded on the Firmware page as an install image. Upgrade images are a separate list and are not offered.
  • Optional: an IPAM backend and a DNS backend in Settings › DNS Records, if you want SATOM to allocate the address or publish the hostname.

ℹ️Note — No hypervisor registered

With no enabled hypervisor the page shows "No hypervisor is registered" and the Mode list offers only Config only. The page itself stays available.

Permissions#

Action Gate in code Granular key that is meant
Open the page, the run detail and the run list operations.view operations.view
Create a run, Preflight, Run / Resume, Roll back coarse config_write operations.apply
  • The Automation menu group, and therefore the Device Provisioning entry, is drawn only for users whose profile grants config_write. That coarse key is unlocked by any of operations.apply, operations.template_save, operations.template_apply, operations.template_approve, protection.edit, protection.apply, network.edit, network.apply, appliances.edit or appliances.apply, so the gate is broader than the one key it is meant for. The built-in Operator and Administrator profiles have it; Viewer does not.
  • A user without config_write does not see the menu entry. With operations.view they can still open /device-provisioning/ by URL and see the runs of the current ADOM; without it the page, run detail and run list answer 403 Forbidden. For such a user the page hides New machine, and the Runs table shows read-only instead of the Preflight, Run and Roll back buttons.
  • Registering, testing and deleting hypervisors in Settings is administrator-only (users.manage).

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: the Device Provisioning page, run detail and run list now require operations.view; signing in alone is no longer enough. The action buttons are only shown to users who may use them, a refused or failed Preflight is shown as an error, and Resume on a paused Semi run now continues to registration.

How to use#

Create a run#

  1. Open Administrator → Devices → Device Provisioning (without users.manage: Automation → Device Provisioning). The entry is only in the menu while a hypervisor is registered and enabled (Settings → Hypervisors); without one the page still opens at /device-provisioning/.
  2. Click New machine. The New machine form opens.
  3. Fill in the fields (see Configuration). Machine name is required.
  4. In the Global ADOM, pick the Product. In a product ADOM the product is that ADOM and cannot be changed.
  5. Click Create run. The form answers "Run created. Press Preflight to see what it will be able to do before anything changes." and the run appears in Runs with status draft.

Check it with Preflight#

  1. In Runs, click Preflight on the run.
  2. Read the result under the form: - Plan: the steps this mode will perform, in order. - Blocked: reasons the run cannot finish. Run will be refused. - Warnings: things that will need a manual action. - "Nothing blocks this run." when there is neither. - "Preflight did not run:" followed by the reason when the server refused the request or failed. That is not a verdict on the run.

Preflight only reads the hypervisor's capabilities. It changes nothing and can be pressed at any time. Modes that do not touch a hypervisor (Config only) always pass.

Run it#

  1. Click Run. SATOM repeats the preflight check first; when it finds a blocker the run is refused with "preflight refused this run" and the blockers are listed.
  2. Otherwise the planned steps execute one after another in that single press, until the plan ends, a step fails, or the mode stops by design.
  3. Watch Step, Progress and Status in the Runs table. Click the run name to open its detail page.
Status Meaning What to do
draft Created, nothing run yet. Preflight, then Run.
running Steps are executing. Wait.
paused The mode stopped where it is designed to stop. The reason is shown. Read the reason. For Semi, complete the first-boot dialog and press Resume.
failed A step failed. The error is shown under the status. Fix the cause and press Run again: the run retries the failed step.
done The plan completed. The appliance is registered (except in VM only).
aborted The run was rolled back. Nothing; it can no longer run.

Read the run detail#

Click a run name. The detail page shows:

  • the mode, current step, status and address;
  • the current error or pause reason (yellow when paused, red otherwise);
  • Pipeline: every step of the pipeline as a badge. Greyed steps are not part of this mode's plan — "they are skipped by design, not failures.";
  • Run log: one row per step attempt and rollback action (Step, OK, Detail, At), newest first.

The detail page has no action buttons; use the Runs table.

Roll a run back#

  1. In Runs, click Roll back. The button changes to Confirm roll back for four seconds.
  2. Click Confirm roll back.
  3. The run becomes aborted. Its log lists what was removed.

⚠️Warning — Roll back is offered on finished runs too

Roll back is shown for every run that is not already aborted, including done runs. On a done run it still deletes the virtual machine SATOM created, the DNS record it published and the address it allocated from IPAM.

Modes#

The plan of each mode is fixed in code. A step not in the plan is skipped.

Mode Plan Hypervisor needs
Full ip_reserved → dns_created → vm_created → image_attached → booted → reachable → onboarded → cert_installed → profile_applied → done create VMs, power control, scriptable serial console
Semi ip_reserved → dns_created → vm_created → image_attached → booted, then pauses; Resume continues reachable → onboarded → cert_installed → profile_applied → done create VMs, power control
DHCP dns_created → vm_created → image_attached → booted → reachable → onboarded → cert_installed → profile_applied → done create VMs, power control
VM only vm_created → image_attached → booted, then pauses create VMs, power control
Config only ip_reserved → dns_created → reachable → onboarded → cert_installed → profile_applied → done none

What each step does in this release:

Step Behaviour
ip_reserved Uses the Management address you typed. If Take the address from IPAM is ticked, asks the IPAM backend instead and records the reservation. Fails if neither is given.
dns_created Skipped when Hostname (DNS) is empty. With no DNS backend configured it passes but logs "NO DNS BACKEND IS CONFIGURED — no record was created …" with the record to add by hand. Fails without an address, or when the backend cannot or will not write the record.
vm_created Creates the machine with the name, vCPU, memory, disk, node, datastore and network given (empty placement fields fall back to the hypervisor's defaults) and a serial port.
image_attached The install image is attached during creation; this step records that. Without an image the machine has an empty disk.
booted Powers the machine on.
reachable Opens a TCP connection to the management address on 443, 8443, then 22 (4 seconds each).
onboarded Registers an appliance named after the run, with the address, the run's product as its kind, Admin user and Admin password to set as its credentials, and TLS verification off.
cert_installed No action: logs "certificate step is a no-op until a CA profile is selected for this run".
profile_applied No action. Without a system profile on the run it logs "no system profile selected — configuration left to the operator"; with one it only hands over: "ready for profile #<id> — apply it from Provisioning with dry-run and approval".

❗Important — What the modes do not do in this release

The mode table on the page says the same: - Full has no step that drives the first-boot dialog: "The first-boot dialog is not scripted: the appliance must come up on that address by itself (for example from a pre-configured image)." After booted the run goes straight to reachable, which fails until the appliance answers on its management address. Complete the first-boot dialog on the console and press Run again. - DHCP does not discover the leased address: "SATOM then probes the management address entered on the run … It does not discover the lease." Enter the address of the machine's DHCP reservation on the run. dns_created fails if a hostname is given without an address. - No mode configures the appliance — not Full, not Config only. In every mode the certificate step is a no-op and the profile step only hands over to System Provisioning. Apply a profile afterwards from System Provisioning, with its dry run, approval and per-device {{ variables }}. - Admin password to set is not written to the appliance; it is stored as the password SATOM uses to log in to it.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Machine name Name of the virtual machine and of the registered appliance. Yes fweb-01
Mode One of the five modes above. Default Semi. Only Config only is offered when no hypervisor is enabled. Yes Semi
Hypervisor Enabled hypervisor to build on. — none (config only) — is valid only for Config only. For all modes except Config only hv-lab (proxmox)
Install image An install firmware image of this ADOM's product. No — none —
Product Only in the Global ADOM: the product being built. Decides the kind of appliance registered. Yes, in Global FortiWeb
Hostname (DNS) Name to publish as an A record. No fweb-01.example.com
Management address Address of the appliance. Unless IPAM is ticked 192.0.2.10
Netmask Netmask of the management address (an IPAM answer overrides it when it returns one). No 255.255.255.0
Gateway Default gateway (an IPAM answer overrides it when it returns one). No 192.0.2.1
vCPU Virtual CPUs. Non-numbers fall back to 4. No 4
Memory (MB) Memory. Non-numbers fall back to 4096. No 4096
Disk (GB) Disk size; 0 = from image. No 0
Node / Datastore / Network Placement on the hypervisor. Empty uses the hypervisor's saved defaults. No —
Admin user Account SATOM uses for the registered appliance. Default admin. No admin
Admin password to set Stored encrypted and used as the appliance's password at registration. No —
Take the address from IPAM Allocate the address from the IPAM backend. Only an address allocated this way is released on roll back. No ticked

Example#

🧪Example — Config only for a physical appliance

A FortiWeb appliance was racked and given 192.0.2.10 on its console. No hypervisor is involved.

  1. In the FortiWeb ADOM, open Administrator → Devices → Device Provisioning and click New machine.
  2. Machine name fweb-01, Mode Config only, Hostname fweb-01.example.com, Management address 192.0.2.10, Admin user admin, Admin password to set: the password configured on the console.
  3. Create run, then Preflight: "Nothing blocks this run."
  4. Run. The log shows ip_reserved (using the supplied address 192.0.2.10), dns_created, reachable (192.0.2.10:443 answered), onboarded (registered appliance #… (fortiweb)), the two no-op steps, and done.
  5. fweb-01 now appears in Appliances. Apply a system profile to it from System Provisioning.

Result#

  • Creating, running and rolling back a run each write an audit log entry (provision.device.create, provision.device.advance, provision.device.rollback). Preflight is not audited.
  • The onboarded step adds a row to Appliances. A roll back leaves that appliance registered on purpose and says so in the run log — remove it from Appliances if you do not want it.
  • The POST actions on this page go through SATOM's device-job mechanism: an action that takes longer than the inline window shows in the job dock and on the Jobs page.

Troubleshooting#

"a machine name is required"#

Possible causes - Machine name was left empty.

Solution 1. Enter a name and click Create run again.

Verification - The run appears in Runs as draft.

"that mode needs a hypervisor"#

Possible causes - A mode other than Config only was chosen with — none (config only) — as the hypervisor. - The chosen hypervisor was disabled after the page loaded.

Solution 1. Pick an enabled hypervisor, or switch the mode to Config only. 2. If none is listed, ask an administrator to register one in Settings › Hypervisors.

Verification - Create run succeeds.

"pick the product this appliance will be"#

Possible causes - The run was created in the Global ADOM without choosing Product.

Solution 1. Select the product in Product, or create the run from inside that product's ADOM.

Verification - The run is created and shows in that product's ADOM.

"preflight refused this run"#

Possible causes - "no hypervisor selected — pick one, or use the 'Config only' mode against a machine that already exists". - "hypervisor unreachable: …" — SATOM could not query the hypervisor. - " cannot drive the first-boot console unattended" — Full on a host without a scriptable serial console (for example ESXi). - " cannot create virtual machines" or "… cannot power machines on and off".

Solution 1. Press Preflight to see the full list of blockers. 2. Fix the hypervisor side, or create a new run with a mode the host supports (for example Semi instead of Full). The mode of an existing run cannot be changed.

Verification - Preflight shows no Blocked: section and Run proceeds.

"this run is finished"#

Possible causes - Run was sent for a run that is done or aborted.

Solution 1. Create a new run.

Verification - The new run is listed as draft.

Run failed at ip_reserved#

Possible causes - "no management address given and IPAM allocation was not requested for this run". - "IPAM allocation was requested but no enabled backend carries the IPAM role (Settings -> DNS Records)". - The IPAM backend did not answer, cannot hand out addresses, or refused.

Solution 1. Roll the run back and create a new one with a Management address, or 2. Have an administrator configure an IPAM backend, then press Run again.

Verification - The log shows ip_reserved with ok.

Run failed at reachable#

Possible causes - "… is not answering on 443, 8443 or 22 — if the first-boot dialog has not been completed yet, do that and resume". - The appliance is still booting, has no address yet, or the address entered is not the one it uses.

Solution 1. Complete the first-boot dialog on the hypervisor console and set the management address you entered in the run. 2. Press Run. The run retries reachable.

Verification - The log shows <address>:443 answered (or 8443 / 22).

A paused Semi run fails at reachable after Resume#

Possible causes - Resume continues the Semi run with reachable, which probes the management address of the run. The first-boot dialog was not completed yet, or it set a different address.

Solution 1. Finish the first-boot dialog on the hypervisor console, with the management address and admin password entered on the run. 2. Press Run. The run retries reachable, then registers the appliance.

Verification - The run ends done and the appliance appears in Appliances.

"Preflight did not run: HTTP 403 …" or the Runs table shows "read-only"#

Possible causes - Your profile does not grant config_write, so the server refuses Preflight, Run and Roll back.

Solution 1. Ask an administrator for operations.apply (see Users and profiles).

Verification - The Automation group appears in your menu, New machine is shown, and Preflight lists a Plan:.

Roll back left items behind#

Possible causes - "hypervisor target is gone — the machine … must be removed by hand". - "could not delete the machine: …", "could not remove the DNS record: …" or "could not release the address: …".

Solution 1. Read the run's error and its Run log rows starting with rollback:. 2. Remove the named items by hand on the hypervisor, DNS or IPAM system.

Verification - The external system no longer holds the machine, record or address.

Advanced#

Advanced Where things are stored
  • Runs are kept in the provision_runs table; hypervisors in hypervisor_targets. Both are created automatically at start-up.
  • The admin password and hypervisor secrets are stored encrypted.
  • Each run keeps the last 200 log entries; each entry's detail is cut at 2,000 characters.
  • The page lists the 50 most recent runs of the current ADOM. The same list is available as JSON at /device-provisioning/data (scope, runs, has_hypervisor).
  • The run's product is taken from the ADOM of the request, never from the form, except in the Global ADOM where the Product field is required.
Advanced What roll back relies on

Roll back acts only on facts recorded by the run: - the virtual machine is deleted only if the run stored a machine handle when it created it; - the DNS record is deleted through the backend that created it; - the address is released only if it was allocated from IPAM, using the reservation handle recorded at allocation. A typed address is never released.

Because runs hold these handles, an administrator cannot delete a hypervisor or a DNS/IPAM backend while a run that is neither done nor aborted still references it.

Advanced Inputs the form does not expose

The create endpoint also accepts profile_id and ip_pool, but the page has no field for them. With no pool, IPAM uses its configured default. A profile_id does not apply anything: the profile_applied step only logs that the profile is ready to be applied from System Provisioning.
